clue.text: Work wearing which item of headgear?

indicators.note: wearing puts the word for work on the inside, as clothing goes round the body

parts.note: which can be replaced by that as a relative pronoun
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which hat to put on for the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat worn with formal dress is a classic item of headgear.

clue.text: Educated firm in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: firm in the sense of tight or tense means taut

explanation.surface: A school or college described as a solid concern, as judged by those listening in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been instructed or schooled has been educated, the past participle of teach.

clue.text: Quiet donkey transported green traveller

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: transported means carried off or moved about, so these letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A silent donkey carries an inexperienced traveller along.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is a person travelling in a vehicle without driving it, so a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Removing coat in Savoy, rogue has duck and fruit

indicators.note: taking the coat off a word strips its outer letters, leaving only the inside

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: In the Savoy hotel, a rascal takes off his jacket and orders duck with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is a famous London hotel, which makes the dining picture feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, eaten as a savoury.

clue.text: Opponent of article by Observer with no content

parts.note: an article in the sense of a thing or item is an object

indicators.note: a word with no content has its inside emptied, keeping just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a piece in the Observer newspaper because it says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, so 'article' tempts as a news piece; here it means a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raises an objection is set against something, so an opponent of it.

clue.text: Lay belching, unhappily complaining

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things going wrong, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone lay there burping, miserable and grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellyaching is informal for grumbling or moaning, a colloquial word for complaining.

clue.text: Indie to supply version

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, supply means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An independent record label is asked to provide a release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but read as 'in a supple way' it signals the rearrangement of INDIETO.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one particular form in which a book or recording is issued, so a version.

clue.text: Angrily slate product sold by Musk

indicators.note: angrily implies being stirred up, so the letters of slate are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone furiously criticises an item sold by Elon Musk.
explanation.walkthrough: To slate is British for criticising harshly, which suits the angry surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesla electric cars are made by the company run by Elon Musk, so a product he sells.

clue.text: Move extremely rare badger's home next to walls of lodge

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: a sett is the burrow where badgers live

indicators.note: the walls of a building are its outside, so take the outer letters of lodge

explanation.surface: Relocating a badger's den next to a lodge, which very rarely happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to move to or set up in a new place, so to relocate.

clue.text: Escalates contentious conclusion

parts.note: escalates in the sense of increases means ups, as in ups the stakes
a hot topic is a contentious one

explanation.surface: A heated dispute grows until it reaches its controversial ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or result of something, so its conclusion.

clue.text: Finally she will sell deli top ingredients — Thai lemongrass …

indicators.note: finally points at the final letter of each of the following words in turn

parts.words: she will sell deli top ingredients — Thai lemongrass

explanation.surface: A shop note trailing off mid-list about a deli's best ingredients for Thai cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the trailing dots themselves, the punctuation mark that shows the sentence is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots marking an omission or trailing off form the punctuation mark of that name.

clue.text: Greeting new archery ranking

parts.note: hi is a casual greeting

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version of the word, so its letters are remade in another order

explanation.surface: Welcome to the latest league table for archers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is a system of grades ranked one above another, a ranking.

clue.text: Limited last bit of traffic on street — direct all over the place

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters of direct are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traffic on a street is restricted, and a chaotic diversion follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constricted is squeezed or restricted, so limited in scope or space.

clue.text: Liquid paint is unsuitable

indicators.note: liquid suggests something fluid and changeable, so the letters of paint flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Runny paint is no good for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means not appropriate or fitting, so it is a synonym of unsuitable.

clue.text: Golf, eighteen holes by key base in Houston

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a full round of golf is played over eighteen holes
CONTROL is the Ctrl key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a round and then heads for the key headquarters in Houston.
explanation.walkthrough: Mission Control in Houston, Texas guides NASA spaceflights; 'Golf' and 'eighteen holes' make the golf story the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground control is the team on Earth directing a spaceflight, famously the NASA centre at Houston.

clue.text: Repairing and putting away again?

definitions.meaning: mending or bringing back to a former condition
stowing in a store a second time, the question mark flagging the split into re- and storing

explanation.definitionFit: Restoration is repair work, and broken as re-storing it means stashing goods once more.

clue.text: Endless festival danger for star

indicators.note: endless means the word loses both of its end letters, front and back

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival
a risk is a danger or hazard

explanation.surface: An unending celebration carries peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' usually trims one end; here it removes both, so the Christian spring festival loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped typographic symbol, from the Greek for little star.

clue.text: Grasp right lines soliloquising, capturing vitality

indicators.note: capturing means the words hold the answer within them, running through all four

explanation.surface: An actor learns the correct lines for a soliloquy, getting the energy right.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightliness is liveliness and energy, so a synonym of vitality.

clue.text: Seabird that is originally seen in channels

parts.note: a gull is a common seabird
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: originally points at the origin or start of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A gull, it seems, was first spotted in the waterways.
explanation.definitionFit: Gullies are narrow channels or ravines cut by running water.

clue.text: Raise section of steel bonnet from the bottom

indicators.note: from the bottom says the hidden letters are read backwards
a section of something is a piece cut from it, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lift a panel of a car's steel bonnet from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'section' into the definition, but 'section of' is the hidden-word signal and 'Raise' alone is the definition; reading up the down light reverses ELBONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, elevating their rank.

clue.text: Part of Himalayas' central climb

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of the central Himalayas is a mountaineer's climb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is the act of going up a mountain, so a climb.

clue.text: Throw out old paella regularly

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of paella is taken

explanation.surface: Get rid of stale paella on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force out or eject, so to throw out.

clue.text: Former member of a religious order

definitions.meaning: a monk ranking just below an abbot, or heading a priory

explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, and a prior is a monk heading a religious house.

clue.text: Frank's in class checking ordinary uniform

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: checking means holding back or stopping, so the word for class holds the two letters within it

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind, especially in biology
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Frank, in class, is inspecting a normal school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' reads as a pupil's name, but it is the adjective; the 's is 'is'. O and U sit inside GENUS after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuous means innocently candid and open, so frank or artless.

clue.text: Start single egg before one brewed tea

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a nit is the egg of a louse
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: brewed means stewed or mixed, so the letters of tea are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Begin with one egg, then make a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin it, so to start it.

clue.text: Compel flying from time to time wearing medal

indicators.note: wearing means the honour goes around the other letters like something worn

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: from time to time means now and then, so every other letter of flying is taken

explanation.surface: Someone forced to fly occasionally while wearing a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' looks like an action in the story, but it only supplies letters; the OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to bind or force them to do something, so to compel.

clue.text: Reportedly hold back team in road border

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: to curb is to hold back or restrain
a side is a team, as in a football side

explanation.surface: A team is said to be held up at the edge of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: KERB is the British spelling of the American curb, the edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerbside is the edge of the road beside the pavement, its border.

clue.text: Force of women's crew

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women or women's, as on clothing labels
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: The strength of a women's rowing team.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight is the downward force that gravity exerts on a mass.
